**Continued 2.4.0**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continued is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continued`), keeps reading your existing `~/.continue` configuration, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.2.0, install the new `.vsix` the same way; your settings are kept.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continued-<platform>-2.4.0.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continued/blob/main/docs/continued-install.md).

| Platform                    | File                                                                   |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continued-win32-x64-2.4.0.vsix`, `continued-win32-arm64-2.4.0.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continued-darwin-arm64-2.4.0.vsix`, `continued-darwin-x64-2.4.0.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continued-linux-x64-2.4.0.vsix`, `continued-linux-arm64-2.4.0.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continued-<platform>-2.4.0-agents.vsix`. It adds Continued to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continued`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continued/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

The Linux armhf and Alpine packages of 2.2.0 are gone: their native modules were built for other platforms and did not work.

## What's new since 2.2.0

**Agents**

- Subagents: agent definitions in `.continue/agents/` (and Claude Code's `.claude/agents/`), a Subagent tool, and a card for each run with its status, model, tokens, approvals and Stop. Up to three run at once, and only one at a time on a local server that serves one request at a time.
- Plan mode ends with a saved plan file and **Build** / **Keep planning**. Plan mode asks before tools that may make changes, MCP tools included.
- Task lists kept with the session: the agent's list stays at the end of each request, so compaction or trimming does not lose its place.
- Messages typed while the agent works are queued and saved with the session. **Send now** steers a queued message into the running turn at the next tool boundary.

**VS Code integration**

- Continued's models appear in VS Code's own model picker, and its MCP servers in VS Code's MCP server list (`continue.shareModelsWithVSCode`, `continue.shareMcpServersWithVSCode`).
- The agents build adds Continued to the Agents window (see above).

**Local model servers**

- A **Local server (OpenAI-compatible)** entry in provider setup, for Strata, llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio, Ollama and others. **Detect** finds running servers on the usual ports, and the saved models get the context window, tool support and image support the server reports. See [Local servers](https://b1tninja.github.io/continued/customize/model-providers/more/local-servers).
- While a llama.cpp or Strata server reads a long prompt, the toolbar shows how far it is, how much came from its cache and about how long is left.
- Warnings before a change would make a local server read the whole conversation again (switching mode or model, changing tools, compacting), with the expected time at the server's last speed, and a notice when it did not use its cache, with the likely cause.

**Prompt caching**

- The start of the prompt stays the same between requests: matched rules stay in place, tools are in a fixed order, rule and skill lists are sorted, and long conversations are trimmed in steps instead of a little on every request. Fewer cache misses on Anthropic, Bedrock and local servers.
- A warning before compacting a cached conversation.

**Providers and models**

- A model catalog: define each model once in `~/.continue/models.yaml` (or a workspace's `.continue/models.yaml`) with the account that serves it, and use it in any config with `from: Name`. Models from different accounts mix freely by role and mode, for example a local model for Agent mode and Claude on Bedrock for Plan mode. See [Model catalog](https://b1tninja.github.io/continued/customize/model-catalog).
- Set up models writes the account to `providers.yaml`, the models to the catalog and a `from:` entry to the config. **Turn into an account** converts a connection set up before, and **Assign models** sets every model's roles (Chat, Edit, Apply, Autocomplete, Subagents, Compaction) in one table.
- Variants: `Name#variant` changes a model's settings, not which model it is. Setup adds one per reasoning effort a llama.cpp or Strata server reports, and switching between them does not warn about the prompt cache.
- Routes: one model served by several accounts, tried in order when one is unreachable, refuses the key, or is throttled or unavailable. The usage readout says which account answered, and a failed account is skipped for a few minutes.
- Retries: rate limits and overloaded servers are retried by one policy that follows the server's `Retry-After`; a server that does not answer fails after 10 seconds (`requestOptions.connectTimeout`); and when the tries run out the chat keeps your message, says what happened and offers to try again.
- Provider accounts: manage provider keys in one place, and move keys kept in plain text in `config.yaml` to secure storage.
- Tab autocomplete works on Bedrock models.

**Other**

- Markdown tables no longer crash chat replies.
- The chat fits narrow and short panels.
- The extension activates when Windows Smart App Control blocks a native module.
- Help links, issue forms and the docs site point at this repository. The docs are at [b1tninja.github.io/continued](https://b1tninja.github.io/continued/).
- Dependencies brought up to date and security alerts addressed.

## Not included

The upstream CLI (`cn`), the JetBrains plugin and the hosted Continue Hub are not part of Continued. Hub `uses: owner/name` blocks are not supported; configure models and blocks directly or with local file paths.
